newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar capped in Singapore ahead of U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar capped in Singapore ahead of U.S. jobs data.

text.p: The dollar showed a firmer bias in Asian trading but will have trouble scaling any key levels ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls data for July, due later on Friday, Singapore dealers said.
They said the dollar had been lifted by U.S. fund buying from the 118.55/60 yen level just after lunch but exporter offers were expected near the key technical 119.00 yen.
"On the the first try, it probably won't go to 119 yen. It will come off a bit but I think it will go through after the (payrolls) figure," a European bank dealer said.

The consensus forecast in a Reuters survey calls for a non-farm payrolls figure of 193,000 in July versus 217,000 in June, while the overall unemployment rate is expected to edge down 0.1 point to 4.9 percent.
Activity in dollar/mark was largely a function of the mark crosses but dealers said there appeared to be some dollar sell orders around 1.8440/50 marks.
"Above the 1.8450 mark level, I believe there are some stop-loss buy orders. The market still wants to long the dollar. People are looking at 1.90 eventually," the dealer said.
